bc_nesakwatch_spires_chew_the_nuun.skip_reason: Route page gives only 'see topo' for its start and the line was not completed to a top; no source says where it ends or how to get off.

set.descent_text: From the summit block, follow cairns along the ridge to a rappel anchor; a single rappel drops into the notch between South Spire and Rexford. Descend the steep sandy gully from the notch, class 2 to 3 or snow-filled early in the season, back to the basin.
set.approach: The spires are reached from the Nesakwatch Creek forest road, whose washouts and slides change from year to year, so check current access before driving. From where you park, walk the road past the washouts to the trail, which is easy to miss. It climbs steeply through forest and an old cutblock to a large granite wall, then bears right and up onto granite slabs and into the basin, where boulders make good bivouacs. Dairyland climbs the South Spire's west side.

review.notes: Route page for the summit finish on the west face; Fairytales page and the Nesakwatch trip report agree on the cairned ridge, single rappel to the notch and the gully; area page and trip report for the approach.

set.descent_text: The last pitch scrambles to the col between the North and South Spires. From the col between the two spires, drop west on fourth-class and low fifth-class ledges and steps, passing a ledge that looks like a bivouac site, to rappel stations that reach the ground, then follow the path back to the basin.
set.approach: From the camp basin, walk toward the South Spire; the route lies left of the climb called Frog Face. Go up a ramp and traverse left, with care, to the foot of a wide chimney. It is a tight squeeze, so a party of three might start lower and scramble into it.

review.notes: Route page for the col finish and start; Waltz Right In and the SW ridge trip report for the westward descent from the col with rappels below it.

set.descent_text: The traverse finishes on Rexford. Descend its west ridge, easy ridge walking on heather and granite blocks, following cairns to a gully; this is snow-filled early in the season, and it leads down between the South Spire and Rexford to the basin.
set.approach: The spires are reached from the Nesakwatch Creek forest road, whose washouts and slides change from year to year, so check current access before driving. From where you park, walk the road past the washouts to the trail, which is easy to miss. It climbs steeply through forest and an old cutblock to a large granite wall, then bears right and up onto granite slabs and into the basin, where boulders make good bivouacs. The traverse begins on the north ridge of the North Spire.

review.notes: Route page and trip report agree on the linkage (north ridge of North Spire, south ridge down, north ridge of South Spire, rappel, northwest face of Rexford, west ridge down). Trip report for the west-ridge descent and the gully.

set.descent_text: The route ends on the summit of the North Spire. From the summit, downclimb fourth-class blocks to the southeast and pick up a worn path between boulders that slants down the ridge's eastern flank to the low point between the spires. Early in the season snow on this ridge can make it hazardous. From the col between the two spires, drop west on fourth-class and low fifth-class ledges and steps, passing a ledge that looks like a bivouac site, to rappel stations that reach the ground, then follow the path back to the basin. That descent lands on the Nesakwatch Creek side, not the Centre Creek side where the climb started.
set.approach: Approach from Centre Creek instead of the Nesakwatch road. Ford the creek, then go up a snow gully into the basin, the same way as the Rexford north face. Head right toward the northeast rib of the North Spire and aim for the big cleft. The route depends on snow through the notch, so conditions matter.

review.notes: Route page for the Centre Creek approach and finish on the summit (seb page confirms the snow gully approach); descent from Waltz, SW ridge and North Ridge pages. Rated rarely repeated, so only the page's own facts are used.

bc_nesakwatch_spires_north_nesakwatch_sp.skip_reason: Page gives only 'see topo' and the line on the west ridge's left flank; no source says where it tops out or where the base is.

set.descent_text: The route reaches the summit by the upper west ridge. From the summit, downclimb fourth-class blocks to the southeast and pick up a worn path between boulders that slants down the ridge's eastern flank to the low point between the spires. Early in the season snow on this ridge can make it hazardous. From the col between the two spires, drop west on fourth-class and low fifth-class ledges and steps, passing a ledge that looks like a bivouac site, to rappel stations that reach the ground, then follow the path back to the basin.
set.approach: The spires are reached from the Nesakwatch Creek forest road, whose washouts and slides change from year to year, so check current access before driving. From where you park, walk the road past the washouts to the trail, which is easy to miss. It climbs steeply through forest and an old cutblock to a large granite wall, then bears right and up onto granite slabs and into the basin, where boulders make good bivouacs. The main trail comes up into the talus field under the northwest face; from its base a diagonal ramp of fourth-class rock and snow leads to the upper west ridge. In early season bring crampons and an ice axe.

review.notes: Route page for the ramp and early-season gear; Waltz Right In for the talus field below the northwest face; descent from Waltz, SW ridge and North Ridge pages.

set.descent_text: The route ends on the summit. The descent follows easy terrain down the south ridge of the spire to the col, and snow can make that ridge hazardous in early season. An old rappel route also winds down the south face and may be preferable depending on conditions. From the col between the two spires, drop west on fourth-class and low fifth-class ledges and steps, passing a ledge that looks like a bivouac site, to rappel stations that reach the ground, then follow the path back to the basin.
set.approach: From the basin, cross to the low fifth-class chimneys at the foot of the spire's southwest side. Either rope up there or scramble to the base of the first pitch, which starts from a dead tree and has cracks with a few fixed pieces.

review.notes: Route page for the descent and start; trip reports agree on south ridge descent, snow, and rappels below the col; Waltz for the ledges west of the col.

bc_nesakwatch_spires_soscratchmewhere.skip_reason: Page places it only 'near the col' with a topo; the descent is a rappel from a tree or a walk-off with no landmark, so no usable text.

set.descent_text: The route ends on the South Spire; the summit block has an offwidth. From the summit block, follow cairns along the ridge to a rappel anchor; a single rappel drops into the notch between South Spire and Rexford. Descend the steep sandy gully from the notch, class 2 to 3 or snow-filled early in the season, back to the basin. This lands on the Nesakwatch Creek side, so a party that started from Centre Creek needs a way back to that vehicle.
set.approach: Approach from Centre Creek. Ford it and go up the snow gully, toward the Priest-Coupe couloir that separates Rexford from the South Spire. Where the couloir meets its bergschrund, step right onto the rock. Crampons and ice axes are required, and the route is best early in the season.

review.notes: Route page for approach and ending; Fairytales and trip report for the cairned ridge, single rappel and gully.

set.descent_text: The route ends on the ridge; the summit block, with an offwidth, lies farther north along it. To descend, follow the ridge south to a single bolted rappel, cairned, that drops to the notch between South Spire and Rexford. Then take the steep sandy gully, class 2 to 3 or snow, down to the basin.
set.approach: The spires are reached from the Nesakwatch Creek forest road, whose washouts and slides change from year to year, so check current access before driving. From where you park, walk the road past the washouts to the trail, which is easy to miss. It climbs steeply through forest and an old cutblock to a large granite wall, then bears right and up onto granite slabs and into the basin, where boulders make good bivouacs. The route is up the middle of the west face. It begins roughly 40 m under a neat square chimney that flares out into a V shape; scramble a dirty corner to a ledge about 10 m up.

review.notes: Route page for start and descent; trip report for the rappel and snow gully.

set.descent_text: From the top, scramble south or southeast to a rappel station; one rope gets you down onto the south ridge. Scramble from there to the col between South Spire and Rexford, then descend the steep sandy gully, class 2 to 3 or snow-filled early in the season, to the basin.

review.notes: Route page for the rappel to the south ridge and scramble to the col; Fairytales and trip report for the gully. Approach skipped: no source places its base.

set.descent_text: Return to the notch between South Spire and Rexford, where the route starts. A rope can be held fixed from below on the north side of the summit block while the top climber rappels the other side. Then descend the steep sandy gully from the notch, class 2 to 3 or snow-filled early in the season, to the basin. The south-side rappel line used by the enchainment is not the way up.
set.approach: Reach the notch between South Spire and Rexford by the steep sandy gully from the basin, class 2 to 3 or snow-filled early in the season. The route starts right out of the notch, on blocky fourth-class ground.

review.notes: Route page for start, summit block and the warning; Fairytales and trip report for the gully joining the notch.

set.descent_text: The route finishes on the summit ridge. Follow the ridge south to the cairned bolted rappel, which drops to the notch between South Spire and Rexford, then take the steep sandy gully, class 2 to 3 or snow-filled early in the season, down to the basin.
set.approach: The spires are reached from the Nesakwatch Creek forest road, whose washouts and slides change from year to year, so check current access before driving. From where you park, walk the road past the washouts to the trail, which is easy to miss. It climbs steeply through forest and an old cutblock to a large granite wall, then bears right and up onto granite slabs and into the basin, where boulders make good bivouacs. The route is the right-most line on the South Spire's west side. It starts on the right side of the buttress beside the gully, where you scramble into an alcove.

review.notes: Route page for the line and start; descent from Fairytales and the trip report (both end on the ridge).

set.descent_text: The route ends on a large summit ledge. From the summit, downclimb fourth-class blocks to the southeast and pick up a worn path between boulders that slants down the ridge's eastern flank to the low point between the spires. Early in the season snow on this ridge can make it hazardous. From the col between the two spires, drop west on fourth-class and low fifth-class ledges and steps, passing a ledge that looks like a bivouac site, to rappel stations that reach the ground, then follow the path back to the basin.
set.approach: The spires are reached from the Nesakwatch Creek forest road, whose washouts and slides change from year to year, so check current access before driving. From where you park, walk the road past the washouts to the trail, which is easy to miss. It climbs steeply through forest and an old cutblock to a large granite wall, then bears right and up onto granite slabs and into the basin, where boulders make good bivouacs. The route is in the middle of the northwest face of the North Spire. Either climb steep dirt slopes directly up from the trail or traverse in high from the bivouac areas to the south. The main trail arrives at the talus field right below the face.

review.notes: Route page for the start and full descent; SW ridge, North Ridge pages and trip report for the south ridge descent and rappels.
